fields.text: A vision model inventories your closet - every garment it can actually see, numbered, with colour and detail. An LLM stylist builds one outfit for your brief using ONLY those numbered items, citing the inventory number of every piece it picks, and a second LLM turns the slip into a flat-lay prompt that Muse renders from text alone. Then the loop closes twice: a second vision read inventories only what the flat lay actually shows, and a GLM phantom auditor checks both directions - every slip item against the inventory line it cites (a stylist inventing a silk scarf is a phantom), and every rendered garment against the slip (a renderer adding one is a phantom too) - while a Decide judge gives the headline verdict. The inventory is written before any styling happens, so nobody downstream can quietly expand the closet. See recipes/closet-capsule-audit.md.

nodes.name: Closet capsule, phantom-checked - inventory the closet, style from it only, render, audit

fields.text: Three days in a cool city next week: one smart dinner, one gallery afternoon, one travel day with lots of walking. Build ONE hero outfit for the smart dinner from what is already in my closet - nothing new, nothing borrowed - and tell me which pieces re-wear on the other days.

fields.q: You are the closet clerk in a capsule-wardrobe pipeline. Look at this photo of a closet and write a CLOSET INVENTORY in this exact shape: a first line 'Closet:' with the setting you can see (rail, shelves, doors open or closed); then a numbered list of EVERY distinct garment, pair of shoes and accessory you can actually see - one item per line, in the order: tops, layers, bottoms, dresses or suits, shoes, accessories. Each line gives the item type, its colour, its material or pattern if visible, and one distinguishing detail (buttons, collar, stripe, heel, buckle). Count multiples honestly ('two white t-shirts' is one line). List ONLY what you can actually see - do not guess at anything folded away, hidden or cropped out; if you are unsure of a detail, give your best guess and mark it '(?)'. No outfit suggestions, no shopping advice.

nodes.name: Closet inventory - Gemini reads the closet

fields.system: You are a capsule stylist. The input gives an outfit brief first, then a closet inventory: a numbered list of the ONLY clothes that exist. Write an OUTFIT SLIP in this exact shape: a title line naming the occasion from the brief and the outfit's idea in a few words; then a numbered list of 4 to 7 WORN items - each line copies ONE inventory item word for word as closely as you can and ends with its inventory number in parentheses, like '(inventory #3)'. You may ONLY use items on the inventory: inventing a garment, changing an item's colour or material, or assuming basics the inventory does not list (belts, scarves, jewellery, plain tees) is a phantom and forbidden. Then a 'Re-wear:' line naming two slip items and how each works again on a different day of the brief. Then a 'Not worn:' line listing the inventory numbers you left out, so the choice is auditable. Output the slip only, no preamble.

nodes.name: Stylist - GLM styles from the inventory only

fields.system: You write ONE flat-lay photo prompt for an image model, from an outfit slip. The slip lists numbered worn items, each with an inventory number in parentheses. Your prompt must: name every worn item exactly as the slip describes it (drop the inventory numbers and the title), arranged as a neat top-down flat lay on a plain pale linen background, one of each item, nothing else in frame; end with 'Photorealistic clothing flat lay, soft daylight, no people, no text, no extra garments or accessories.' Keep it under 110 words. Output the prompt only, no preamble.

nodes.name: Flat lay - Muse renders the outfit

fields.question: The text is a closet inventory (a numbered list of the only clothes that exist) followed by an outfit slip whose worn items each cite an inventory number. The image is a flat lay that claims to show exactly the slip's worn items. Which verdict fits? 'closet only, complete' means every worn item is visible in the lay, each matches the inventory item its number cites, and nothing else appears. 'phantom item' means the slip or the lay shows a garment that is not on the inventory, or an item whose colour or type contradicts the inventory line its number cites. 'pieces missing' means one or more worn items cannot be found in the lay and there are no phantoms. 'wrong occasion' means the lay is closet-only and complete but the outfit plainly ignores the brief's occasion named in the slip's title. Judge the garments, not the photography.
fields.options:
closet only, complete
phantom item
pieces missing
wrong occasion

fields.q: You are the flat-lay reader in a capsule-wardrobe pipeline. Look at this clothing flat lay and list ONLY the garments, shoes and accessories you can actually see, one per line: item type, colour, material or pattern if visible, and one distinguishing detail. Count each item once. Do not guess at anything hidden underneath another garment - if you are unsure of a detail, give your best guess and mark it '(?)'. Do not compare it to any list; just report what is visibly there.

nodes.name: Flat-lay read-back - Gemini reads the lay

fields.system: You are a phantom auditor. The input gives three texts in order: a closet inventory (numbered items), then the marker 'OUTFIT SLIP:' and an outfit slip whose worn items each cite an inventory number, then the marker 'FLAT-LAY READ-BACK:' and a reader's inventory of a rendered flat lay. Audit in two passes. PASS 1, the plan: for each worn item on the slip, check its cited inventory number exists and the description matches that inventory line - output nothing for matching items yet. PASS 2, the render: output one line per worn item, in slip order, starting 'WORN - ' if a matching garment is visible in the read-back, or 'MISSING - ' if it is not, followed by the item's short name and its inventory number. Then one line per problem found in either pass, starting 'PHANTOM - ' for a slip item whose number is absent or contradicted by the inventory, or a read-back garment that is on neither the slip nor the inventory. End with one line 'Summary: X of Y worn items rendered, Z phantoms.' Judge by the texts only. Output the audit only, no preamble.

nodes.name: Phantom audit - GLM scores both passes
